module: D09-14 Market Share／Entry Barrier／Substitution／Competitive Strategy市占、進入障礙、替代與競爭策略
purpose: Extend the issuer-action lifecycle outside semiconductors and add an explicit failed/suspended strategic-action control.

receipts.action: Smart Scrap Inspection System R&D project using image recognition to classify scrap and optimize EAF parameters; 2025 planned R&D investment NT$13.82m; project submitted for MOEA industrial-upgrading support.
receipts.competitivePositionHypothesis: May improve scrap classification, energy efficiency, process stability and input handling.
receipts.falsification: R&D spending or a government-support application is not evidence of realized cost advantage, margin improvement or durable market-share gain.

receipts.action: AI-based sinter-machine speed control deployed to No.2 sinter machine; company reports approximately 4% yield improvement and 22,000 tonnes annual carbon reduction.
receipts.competitivePositionHypothesis: Operational digitalization may improve yield/cost/carbon efficiency inside the integrated-route constraint.
receipts.falsification: Operational improvement at one process step does not prove industry-level pricing power, company-wide margin durability or stock alpha.

lifecycle.evidence: Foxconn and Lordstown announced a non-binding framework including planned plant purchase, contract manufacturing and possible further vehicle programs.
Foxconn completed acquisition of the Ohio manufacturing facility and signed manufacturing/joint-development agreements; Lordstown became first commercial-vehicle mass-production customer at the site.
Foxconn group agreed to additional common/preferred share investment subject to conditions; only part of the investment was funded.
Lordstown filed for bankruptcy and sued Foxconn; Foxconn financial reporting records the dispute and suspension of remaining investment.
Foxconn officially stated it suspended subsequent good-faith negotiations.

receipts.competitivePositionHypothesis: The original partnership sought faster North American EV capacity and shared-scale economics.
receipts.falsification: A signed partnership, acquired plant and partial implementation can still fail to deliver the intended partner/customer pathway. This does not imply Foxconn's entire EV strategy failed; it is a negative control for the specific Lordstown strategic-action chain.

lifecycleRules: ANNOUNCED != APPROVED != FUNDED != CONSTRUCTION/IMPLEMENTATION != COMMERCIALIZED != SUCCESSFUL
A strategic action may enter PARTIAL_SUCCESS, DELAYED, SUSPENDED, CANCELLED, COUNTERPARTY_FAILURE or RESTRUCTURED states.
Company-wide strategy must not be declared failed because one partnership/action failed.
Post-action share, margin, revenue and stock outcomes are separate outcome clocks and remain closed in this receipt.
crossIndustryEvidence: Steel digitalization actions show D09-14 is not semiconductor-specific.
Foxconn/Lordstown provides a true negative-control lifecycle in which intent and partial implementation do not guarantee the original strategic thesis completes.
The same industry structure can host issuers with different action states, and the same issuer can have simultaneous successful and failed strategic actions.
antiDoubleCountRules: Tung Ho/CSC process changes are D09-14 action states; physical production/capacity effects link to D10 and are not duplicated.
Foxconn/Lordstown announcement clocks link to D11/D17 event research; D09-14 owns the longitudinal strategic-action implementation state.
No action receives a positive or negative stock score until OOS/prospective outcome evidence exists.
Failure/control labels apply to the specific action chain, not the entire issuer or industry.

pitSemantics.revisionRule: Lifecycle transitions append; prior states remain immutable.

reasonNoL4: Cross-industry and failed-action controls strengthen the unique replay contract, but no prospective/OOS test establishes incremental stock-selection or future-position value after controlling for industry structure, capacity, event and fundamentals.
h01Implication: KEEP_SEPARATE evidence is strengthened: D09-14 has a dynamic issuer-action lifecycle and explicit failure states not represented by a static D09-13 industry-state receipt. Scope dedup remains mandatory.
exactNext: BR-056 accumulate independent firm-action receipts with native post-action share/capacity/revenue outcomes, including at least one completed-success and one failed/delayed control on common support.
Preregister outcome windows before opening stock returns or margin/share outcomes.
Run redundancy/ablation versus D09-13, D10 capacity, D11/D17 event timing and D07 fundamentals before any System1/System2 role classification.
